THE CLINICAL PICTURE

A flexible ECG workflow, from acquisition to review.

The custo cardio 300 is a compact ECG acquisition device used with a compatible computer and custo diagnostic software. The supplied brochure describes both resting and exercise ECG applications, interchangeable patient cables and use across compatible workstations. It is useful to specify the complete workflow: acquisition hardware, licensed software, electrodes, reporting and, for exercise testing, a supported treadmill or ergometer.

For professional healthcare use. This overview supports equipment selection; operation requires the current manufacturer instructions and trained clinical staff.

DESIGNED AROUND YOUR WORKFLOW

Practical advantages.
Clearer equipment decisions.

Look beyond a product name. Match the capabilities to the people, space and systems in your facility.

Work closer to the patient

USB and Bluetooth connection options support different room arrangements. Wireless use can reduce the need for a direct device-to-PC cable during acquisition.

Resting and stress applications

One acquisition platform supports two clinical workflows when configured with the appropriate software and compatible exercise equipment.

Check contact quality

An electrode-quality overview helps staff identify contact issues before recording, supporting an orderly patient preparation process.

Flexible patient connections

Interchangeable patient cables and a suction-system connection option allow the setup to be specified around your electrode workflow.

Recording controls within reach

The brochure describes start/stop controls on the device or PC, plus automatic 10-second ECG acquisition for the resting workflow.

Practical cleaning workflow

The enclosure is designed for cleaning and disinfection according to its instructions. Optional custo clean CR3 and CR3 ergo hygiene bags support preparation between patients.

HOW IT IS USED

A supervised workflow,
from preparation to review.

An orientation for buyers and clinical teams. Exact operating steps depend on your supplied equipment and software.

  1. 01

    Configure the workstation

    Install and license the supplied software, check PC requirements and pair or connect the device using the manufacturer’s setup instructions.

  2. 02

    Prepare and check the recording

    Qualified staff verify patient identity, prepare electrode sites, attach the prescribed leads and use the contact-quality display to address poor connections.

  3. 03

    Acquire resting or stress ECG

    Select the prescribed workflow. For stress testing, use the approved treadmill or ergometer setup under qualified clinical supervision and monitor the patient throughout.

  4. 04

    Review, report and reset

    A qualified clinician reviews the recording and software output. Save or export using the configured system, then clean the device and manage accessories according to the instructions for use.

Clinical context

Exercise stress testing evaluates the heart during physical effort. Patient selection, monitoring and interpretation belong to the responsible clinical team. Patients should follow their clinician’s preparation instructions and should not change medication on the basis of this page. Read the American Heart Association overview ↗

PLAN THE COMPLETE SYSTEM

Specify the software, accessories and exercise device together.

The brochure describes single-beat review, summary complexes, measured-value tables and configurable reporting. For stress ECG, it describes configurable exercise profiles, compatible treadmill/ergometer control and visual or acoustic messages. Ask which features are licensed in your supplied version. BP, SpO₂ and lactate acquisition need suitable connected equipment. CPET expansion needs a separate confirmed configuration. For an existing IT system, request confirmation of the exact export formats and interfaces your facility needs.

Cleaning & ongoing care

Follow the current instructions for use for approved disinfectants, contact times and cleaning technique. Inspect the patient cable, connectors and enclosure before use. Replace single-use electrodes and hygiene bags as instructed. A hygiene bag does not replace the manufacturer’s cleaning process. Confirm replacement cables, consumable availability, battery care and service arrangements before purchase.

YOUR QUESTIONS, ANSWERED

Before you choose.

Practical answers for clinical and procurement teams.

What is the custo cardio 300?

It is a mobile 12-channel ECG acquisition device for resting and stress ECG workflows when used with a compatible computer, diagnostic software and the required accessories.

Does it support wireless ECG acquisition?

The supplied brochure lists Bluetooth as well as USB connectivity. Confirm the supplied connection configuration, compatible workstation and battery arrangements in your quotation.

Can it perform both resting and stress ECG?

Yes, the brochure describes both uses. Your package must include the appropriate software licences and, for exercise testing, a compatible treadmill or ergometer and clinical monitoring setup.

How long does the battery last?

The June 2023 brochure states approximately 10 hours. Treat this as a brochure value, not a guaranteed runtime for every workflow, battery condition or supplied configuration.

Is a computer, treadmill or printer included?

The brochure does not establish a standard Fastonmed package. Ask for an itemised quotation that lists the PC, software, exercise device, printer and accessories separately.

What is the custo cardio 300 price in the UAE?

Pricing is by quotation and depends on hardware, software licences, patient cables, accessories and installation requirements. Request a current AED quotation including VAT, delivery and any support charges.

Can it connect to a CARDIO-TRACK treadmill?

Compatibility must be checked for the exact treadmill model, interface, control protocol and custo software version. These two brochures do not independently confirm that pairing.

Can we add CPET or a suction electrode system?

The brochure describes CPET expansion and connection to a suction system. These require separate compatibility checks, accessories or modules; request a confirmed configuration and itemised scope.

Does automatic interpretation replace a clinician?

No. Automated measurements and interpretation are decision-support functions. The responsible qualified clinician must review the ECG and interpret it in the patient’s clinical context.

How do we arrange a demonstration or buy the system?

Send Fastonmed your facility location, resting/stress requirements, existing equipment and desired delivery date. Request a demonstration if available and confirm the complete package before ordering.
